messages.author: 5900eadecec2d82d
messages.subject: Re: novice question - GIS
parts:
On Mon, 22 May 2000 12:12:01 +0100 (BST), Robin Gill wrote:

> >I would have thought that GIS would be a useful tool to support the design
and analysis of surveys (and could provide covariates) but I'm not aware of
any attempts yet to combine them with distance sampling. Any ideas or
suggestions would be welcome!

We at St Andrews are working on a new version of program Distance (version
4). Distance 4 will include an automated survey design tool based on the GIS
component MapObjects (by ESRI - uses shapefiles like ESRI's ArcView) and the
work of one of the PhD students here, Samantha Strindberg. The design tool
lets you generate survey plans based on various designs, and also does
simulations to look at things like coverage probabilities etc. You can
easily print off maps of the survey plans, etc. We will be using a
preliminary version of this software at the advanced distance workshop in the
fall (see http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distanceworkshop/)

In the future, we will be using the GIS tool to extend the functionality in
Distance to include spatial modelling of density (PhD work at St Andrews by
Sharon Hedley). There will also be simulation capabilities which will allow
you to simulate populations of animals in space and look at the performance
of different designs combined with different abundance estimators.

The new version of distance will be on general release around November or
December this year, and will be free to download for non-commercial use. The
GIS-automated design component will be in this release, but we are at present
not sure about the spatial modelling component: depends on time and funding
constraints. We have been funded these past 3 years by two UK research
councils, but this grant has now finished. I will be making an announcement
on the list shortly seeking sponsors for future development of Distance.

Cheers,

- Len Thomas
